## Round 2 (closed 2026-10-21)

Prediction file: spe/predictions/r02.yaml, saved before the run.
Results file: spe/evals/results/r02/r02.json. The run had 4 arms, 40 tickets, and 5 trials per cell.
I scored pass_rates against category_acc.

### Category accuracy

| Arm | Predicted | Null (same as last round) | Actual | Prediction error | Null error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 0.85 | 0.84 | 0.86 | 0.01 | 0.02 |
| B | 0.88 | 0.84 | 0.86 | 0.02 | 0.02 |
| C | 0.90 | 0.84 | 0.80 | 0.10 | 0.04 |
| D | 0.75 | 0.70 | 0.74 | 0.01 | 0.04 |

The mean absolute error of my predictions is 0.035. The mean absolute error of the null is 0.030. The null beat my predictions this round. All of the gap comes from arm C.

### Other predictions

- C priority_acc: I predicted 0.80. C scored 0.71. The miss is 0.09.
- D cost per ticket: I predicted $0.002. D cost $0.004. The miss is 2x.

### Why claims

- B, "shorter prompt keeps focus": Not supported. B tied A on category_acc at 0.86. B scored 0.78 on priority_acc and A scored 0.79. B did cost 18% less than A ($0.009 vs $0.011). The shorter prompt saves money. It did not raise accuracy.
- C, "merged tools cut wrong tool choice": Refuted. C averaged 2.6 tool calls and A averaged 4.1. C never called check_status on 9 outage tickets. The merge removed needed calls along with wrong ones. See F4.
- D, "same design on a smaller model loses about 0.15": Partly supported. D scored 0.12 below A. My own numbers implied a gap of 0.10 (0.85 vs 0.75), so the why and the numbers disagreed before the run. The accuracy number landed within 0.01. The cost number missed. See F5.

### Noise

One ticket is worth 0.025 of accuracy. A and B each rose 0.02 from last round. That is less than one ticket, so I treat it as noise. C fell 0.06 below A, which is about 2.4 tickets. The check_status note explains that drop, so I treat it as real.

### Lesson for the next prediction

My biggest miss was on the arm I expected to win. I predicted that fewer tools would mean fewer wrong calls. I did not check whether fewer tools would also mean fewer right calls. From now on, any prediction that a change cuts tool calls must name the required calls that could drop.

### Inputs for the r03 plan

- B matches A on accuracy at lower cost. B is the cheaper baseline candidate.
- C should not be rerun until check_status is forced on outage tickets.
- D cost should not be judged until retries on tickets over 2,000 words are capped or the tickets are truncated.

### F4. Arm C skips check_status on outage tickets

- Round: r02. Arm: C (merged tools).
- What happened: C never called check_status on 9 outage tickets. The evidence is trials r02-C-T17-1..3, cited in the notes of spe/evals/results/r02/r02.json.
- Effect: C scored 0.80 on category_acc and A scored 0.86. C scored 0.71 on priority_acc and A scored 0.79. C averaged 2.6 tool calls and A averaged 4.1.
- Cause (hypothesis, unverified): The merged tool lets the model settle an outage ticket without looking up status. Priority on outage tickets likely depends on status, which would explain why priority dropped the most.
- Prediction impact: I predicted 0.90 for C. C scored 0.80, which is below the null of 0.84.
- Fix to test: Require a check_status call on any ticket classed as an outage. The other option is to keep check_status as its own tool next to the merged tool.
- Status: open.

### F5. Arm D retries on long tickets and doubles its token use

- Round: r02. Arm: D (smaller model).
- What happened: D retried on tickets over 2,000 words. The retries doubled the tokens on those tickets.
- Effect: D cost $0.004 per ticket. I predicted $0.002. D still costs the least of the four arms.
- Cause: Unknown. The traces must show whether a context limit or an output format error triggers the retries. Check this before r03.
- Fix to test: Truncate or summarize tickets over 2,000 words before D sees them, or cap retries at 1.
- Status: open.
